target_customer: Patients with iron deficiency anemia, starting with women with heavy menstrual bleeding; commercially pharma partners and payers
problem: Oral iron causes GI side effects and IV iron needs infusions and carries risks; the company wants a patch that avoids both.
business_model: Biopharma drug development aiming at licensing or partnering and eventual prescription sales
product_category: Metallodrug and drug delivery patch (NistuFe, KYLK01)

founders.name: Buddhadev P. Chaudhuri
education: PhD Drug Delivery Microsystems, Imec / KU Leuven
founders.background_notes: YC page: about 15 years in healthcare technologies; company site names Biolinq and Koniku.

founders.name: Frederik Ceyssens
founders.background_notes: Schools not named on YC page.

competitors.name: Fe3 Medical
competitors.what: Transdermal iron patch using iontophoresis for iron deficiency anemia, an InCube Labs company
competitors.traction_then: Preclinical and early clinical work; a 2019 study reported therapeutic iron delivery
competitors.funding_then: 11M USD Series B in March 2016, later topped up to 14.5M USD by Texas

competitors.name: Accrufer (Shield Therapeutics)
competitors.what: Oral ferric maltol, FDA approved for iron deficiency in adults

competitors.name: Injectafer (American Regent)
competitors.what: IV iron product approved for pediatric patients in Dec 2021
competitors.funding_then: Part of Daiichi Sankyo group (not sourced here)

technical_complexity.rationale: A new molecular entity with a novel delivery route needs preclinical, regulatory and clinical work well beyond a small team.

defensibility.rationale: A new molecular entity can be patented and approval is hard to replicate, but nothing is proven in humans yet.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents sold oral and IV iron; no sourced action against Keylika.

market_need_then: Company cites about 1.6 billion people with iron deficiency worldwide and over 30 million in the US; oral and IV iron both have known drawbacks.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and promotional with superlatives such as breakthrough, best in class and world's first.

branding.brand_signature: World's first prescription iron patch positioning; product brand NistuFe
branding.community_and_virality: Paid or partner style coverage in 2024 and 2025 (IBTimes, Entrepreneur, Arabian Business, Benzinga partner post); no organic community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Early stage biotech with a hard to spell name and mostly promotional coverage.

pivots.why: Not stated; coverage from April 2025 describes a buccal patch while the YC page still says skin patch

outcome_analysis: Keylika is a one person biotech that joined YC in Summer 2022 to develop an iron patch for iron deficiency anemia. Public sources show animal studies and promotional press in 2024 and 2025 but no priced funding round, clinical trial or exit. The product framing shifted from a skin patch to a buccal patch, and the long timeline of drug development means the outcome is still open.
notes: No funding round is confirmed. Aggregators list about 500K USD from Y Combinator (convertible note, 2022) which is the standard YC deal and is unverified. The site shows investor logos without names. YC page cites a USA Today contributor piece on the bootstrapping story that was not opened. Fe3 Medical competitor is dated 2016 and still operating as of the later coverage seen; its status in 2022 not verified. Name origin search found nothing. The pivot entry is a change in description, dated by coverage, not a stated pivot. Founder education schools for Ceyssens not named. No shutdown found. Completeness pass: the one recorded round rests on a single database (CB Insights lists $500K convertible note and investors Y Combinator and Gaingels; Bouncewatch dates a pre-seed round 2022-08-22 with no amount). No press release found; the amount may be mostly the standard YC deal.
